selected.title: fix(server): lock operator generation state transitions
selected.author: Afloat16
selected.full_inventory_search_source: Global closed-author PR search, merged_at present.
selected.summary_en: Serialize operator retries and cancellations with concurrent generation-state transitions.
selected.summary_zh: 通过行锁协调操作员重试、取消与并发生成状态变更。
selected.technical_value: Re-reads the scoped generation job under the same PostgreSQL row lock used by generation completion, evaluates the transition and updates state within one transaction. Queue operations and audit publication occur after that transaction.
selected.test_evidence: Committed PostgreSQL integration fixtures use isolated schemas, real row locks, gated concurrent requests and lock-wait inspection. They cover retry conflicts after processing or completion, duplicate retries, cancellation racing with completion and simultaneous cancellations.
selected.limitations: The integration suite requires CLAUDE_MEM_TEST_POSTGRES_URL and skips when it is absent. No database-backed test was executed during this review. Queue I/O remains outside the row-lock transaction.
selected.selection_reason: Addresses concurrent state mutation through transactional row-lock discipline, with explicit race-oriented integration fixtures.
selected.review_method: Inspected the exact final merge-commit production and regression-test patches. Test evidence is from committed fixtures, without a fresh execution.
selected.selection_refresh: Newer substantial merge from this project's current batch.

selected.title: fix(restore): refuse newer-schema snapshots before swapping live data
selected.author: Afloat16
selected.full_inventory_search_source: Global closed-author PR search, merged_at present.
selected.summary_en: Reject newer-schema restore snapshots before replacing the healthy live database.
selected.summary_zh: 在替换正常运行的数据库前，拒绝超出当前支持版本的恢复快照。
selected.technical_value: Checks the staged snapshot's PRAGMA user_version against LATEST_SCHEMA_VERSION in the SQLite file-job process before checkpointing or backing up the live database. The staged WAL participates in the compatibility check.
selected.test_evidence: Committed SQLite fixtures verify rejection preserves the live and snapshot bytes, creates no pre-restore copy, leaves a failed pending restore recoverable by the worker and detects a newer schema stamp in the WAL. Older, current and unstamped snapshots remain accepted.
selected.limitations: The preflight checks the schema version stamp and existing SQLite integrity path. This review inspected the fixtures and did not run the restore suite.
selected.selection_reason: Prevents a destructive ordering error in the restore workflow and validates both refusal and compatible-snapshot controls.
selected.review_method: Inspected the exact final merge-commit production and regression-test patches. Test evidence is from committed fixtures, without a fresh execution.
selected.selection_refresh: Newer substantial merge from this project's current batch.

selected.title: fix(sync): remove replica vectors after remote tombstones
selected.author: Afloat16
selected.full_inventory_search_source: Global closed-author PR search, merged_at present.
selected.summary_en: Schedule replica-vector cleanup after committed remote deletions and earlier writes finish.
selected.summary_zh: 远端删除提交且同条目的先前写入完成后，清理副本中的向量片段。
selected.technical_value: Captures the replica's local row ID before deleting a tombstoned origin record, dispatches cleanup only after the SQLite transaction commits and orders it after earlier writes for that row. Local and replicated deletions share a serialized cleanup lane.
selected.test_evidence: Committed fixtures cover observations, summaries and prompts, assert the replica row ID and matching document type, delay an earlier write to test ordering, discard cleanup on rollback and verify a simulated vector-service failure preserves durable sync progress and permits later cleanup.
selected.limitations: Vector cleanup is best effort. Failures are logged and durable synchronization continues, so a failed vector-service deletion can leave fragments until a later cleanup. Tests use an in-memory SQLite store and a simulated vector client, and were not rerun.
selected.selection_reason: Fixes stale search fragments caused by replicated deletions while explicitly covering transaction rollback and write/delete ordering.
selected.review_method: Inspected the exact final merge-commit production and regression-test patches. Test evidence is from committed fixtures, without a fresh execution.
selected.selection_refresh: Newer substantial merge from this project's current batch.

other_accepted.maintainer_pr_description:
Supersedes #1140, #1141, #1142, #1143, #1144, #1145 and #1146 by @Afloat16. Each one edits `docs/ROADMAP.md` and `docs/STATUS.md`, so merging them one at a time would have left each later one in conflict. They're merged together here with the author's commits kept.

- #1140: inline source-map data URLs ignore their fragment, and the scheme and `base64` marker are matched case-insensitively.
- #1141: ZIP directories are recognised from DOS and Unix attributes even without a trailing slash.
- #1142: rejected ASAR names count toward the listing limit.
- #1143: a HAR with a UTF-8 BOM parses.
- #1144: a .NET bundle member can't read into the manifest's bytes.
- #1145: Play can start a Python project's one installed `[project.scripts]` console script from its own environment.
- #1146: Godot and Electron get an absolute project path.

Two fixes on top of the merge:
- #1145 and #1146 each edited the New-project toolchains row in STATUS. It's now one row carrying both additions, not two copies.
- #1146's `launch_tests` module is moved to the end of `outputs.rs`. On Windows an item after it made clippy fail with `items_after_test_module`, which the Linux gate doesn't compile.

**Verified:** the `formats` and `engine` tests (552 in the engine library), clippy for both on Windows, fmt, `cargo xtask wasm` and layers pass on the merged result.

maintainer_acknowledgment.author: danyaberezun
maintainer_acknowledgment.body: Thanks @Afloat16 — the literal-filename fix landed as part of #1137, credited to you as co-author. #1137 rewrote the same `ignoredPaths` function (a fast `--no-index` first pass), so we folded your fix in there rather than merge two competing versions: the first pass reads `./<path>` records from `--stdin -z`, and the index pass keeps arguments (one index scan per batch — `--stdin` rescans the index per path, ~3× slower on large repos) and unquotes git's C-quoted names, so `"`, `\`, control characters and pathspec-looking names stay literal. Your tests for those names came along. Closing this in favour of #1137.

other_accepted.limitations: The final implementation differs from the source PR: the no-index pass uses NUL-delimited stdin, while the index pass uses bounded arguments and C-quoted path decoding. maintainer_acknowledgment.body:
Merged through #6017, thank you @Afloat16! Your four commits landed on main unchanged and under your name (60de7aecb through 810b8a723); the rehost was only needed because the Vercel AI SDK guide took the same `docs.json` line first and this branch doesn't allow maintainer edits. new_adoptions.attribution: The maintainer explicitly credits Afloat16's literal-filename handling and regression cases from #1250 within #1137. The final squash retains the Afloat co-author trailer. Only this contribution is credited, not the complete Linux watcher implementation.
new_adoptions.summary_en: Preserve literal filenames in Git ignore checks and retain the associated regression cases.
new_adoptions.summary_zh: 在 Git 忽略判断中保留字面文件名，并纳入对应回归案例。

maintainer_acknowledgment.author: danyaberezun
maintainer_acknowledgment.body: Thanks @Afloat16 — the literal-filename fix landed as part of #1137, credited to you as co-author. #1137 rewrote the same `ignoredPaths` function (a fast `--no-index` first pass), so we folded your fix in there rather than merge two competing versions: the first pass reads `./<path>` records from `--stdin -z`, and the index pass keeps arguments (one index scan per batch — `--stdin` rescans the index per path, ~3× slower on large repos) and unquotes git's C-quoted names, so `"`, `\`, control characters and pathspec-looking names stay literal. Your tests for those names came along. Closing this in favour of #1137.

new_adoptions.limitations: The final implementation differs from the source PR: the no-index pass uses NUL-delimited stdin, while the index pass uses bounded arguments and C-quoted path decoding. The entire watcher optimization and its performance results are not attributed to Afloat16. No tests were rerun.

human_comments.author: serengil
human_comments.body:
Thanks a lot for taking the time to look into this and for the clear explanation — you're right that
a plain substring check could, in theory, match 2627/2601 appearing inside an object name or value.

In practice, though, this path only runs inside except pyodbc.IntegrityError during 
insert_embeddings, and the embeddings table has no foreign keys or check constraints. The only
IntegrityError that isn't a duplicate would be a NOT NULL violation, which we never trigger because
every column is always filled. So a false match would also need a database, table or column name
containing those exact digits. Given how unlikely that is, I'd rather keep the simpler check than
tie it to pyodbc's exact message format.

I'm going to close this one, but I really appreciate the careful eye. Contributions like this are
very welcome, so please keep them coming!

human_comments.author: danyaberezun
human_comments.body: Thanks @Afloat16 — the literal-filename fix landed as part of #1137, credited to you as co-author. #1137 rewrote the same `ignoredPaths` function (a fast `--no-index` first pass), so we folded your fix in there rather than merge two competing versions: the first pass reads `./<path>` records from `--stdin -z`, and the index pass keeps arguments (one index scan per batch — `--stdin` rescans the index per path, ~3× slower on large repos) and unquotes git's C-quoted names, so `"`, `\`, control characters and pathspec-looking names stay literal. Your tests for those names came along. Closing this in favour of #1137.

maintainer_acknowledgment.author: danyaberezun
maintainer_acknowledgment.body: Thanks @Afloat16 — the literal-filename fix landed as part of #1137, credited to you as co-author. #1137 rewrote the same `ignoredPaths` function (a fast `--no-index` first pass), so we folded your fix in there rather than merge two competing versions: the first pass reads `./<path>` records from `--stdin -z`, and the index pass keeps arguments (one index scan per batch — `--stdin` rescans the index per path, ~3× slower on large repos) and unquotes git's C-quoted names, so `"`, `\`, control characters and pathspec-looking names stay literal. Your tests for those names came along. Closing this in favour of #1137.

new_adoptions.limitations: The final implementation differs from the source PR: the no-index pass uses NUL-delimited stdin, while the index pass uses bounded arguments and C-quoted path decoding. The entire watcher optimization and its performance results are not attributed to Afloat16. No tests were rerun.
